message.content:
This appears to be a CBP ruling on herbal tinctures. Vegetable extracts fall in heading 1302 ("Vegetable saps and extracts; pectic substances... mucilages and thickeners"). Subheading 1302.19 covers other vegetable saps and extracts. Within 1302.19, the HTSUS 10-digit codes are:
- 1302.19.05 (Medicinal use, ginseng...)
- 1302.19.40 (Ginseng extracts)
- 1302.19.91 (Other)
- 1302.19.9100 (Other)

I recall 1302.19.4000 as "Other: Medicinal" and 1302.19.9100 as "Other" ... The structure I remember is 1302.19.05 (Capsicum oleoresin... "Of a kind used for medicinal purposes") → 1302.19.0500 "Medicinal: Ginseng", 1302.19.15 "Other" → 1302.19.1500... I'm unsure of the exact breakdown. Tinctures of echinacea would be classified in 1302.19.91 "Other" if not for medicinal use specified; with the prepared doses they'd be 3004, but this is bulk, so heading 1302. I'll go with 1302.19.9100.

{"hts_code": "1302.19.9100", "reason": "The glycerin-water macerated liquid botanical extracts of echinacea, houttuynia, isatis and Japanese knotweed are vegetable extracts of heading 1302, falling in the residual 'other' vegetable saps and extracts subheading 1302.19."}

predicted_reason: The glycerin-water macerated liquid botanical extracts of echinacea, houttuynia, isatis and Japanese knotweed are vegetable extracts of heading 1302, falling in the residual 'other' vegetable saps and extracts subheading 1302.19.
